title: Synergies Between Anthropogenic Litter and Biopollution in SW Bay of Biscay Rivers Discovered Through Citizen Science: Implications for Conservation
content:
ABSTRACT

Anthropogenic litter and other pollutants are known to contribute to the introduction and settlement of invasive alien species (IAS) in marine settings; however, the relationship between biopollutant IAS and litter in rivers is much less studied. Here, we assessed the degree of association between pollutants and biopollutants in small Bay of Biscay rivers through participatory citizen science. Sanitary litter (disposable wipes) was the most abundant item type, especially downstream of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). A total of 9 aquatic and 19 riverside IAS were reported by citizen scientists. Positive association between the number of aquatic IAS and the number of litter items suggests a role of anthropogenic litter as a transport vector. Moreover, strong correlation between smoking and fishing litter and the number of IAS points to illegal or inadvertent introduction of some species in frequented river zones. Improving WWTP functioning and designing campaigns for public awareness of litter and biological pollution are highly recommended for the conservation of crucial river biodiversity.
